political_geopolitical.key_assumption: The tariff shock will escalate geopolitical tensions and trigger a significant risk-off sentiment in markets.
supporting_evidence: Geopolitical Risk Premium (score 68.0): Elevated pre-event GPR index (142 vs avg 103) suggests heightened sensitivity to geopolitical shocks.
Sanctions / Trade / Policy Shock (score 96.0): Event directly matches the channel, with sector-specific rates and immediate implementation timeline.
transmission_channels: Geopolitical Risk Premium → risk-off sentiment → broad market decline
Sanctions / Trade / Policy Shock → policy uncertainty → sector-specific underperformance (XLF, XLK)
Safe-Haven / FX Flow → USD appreciation → further pressure on equities

channel_assessment.channel_adjustments: The April 2025 regime, with elevated GPR (142), indicates a heightened sensitivity to geopolitical shocks compared to historical analogues.

economic_fiscal_market.key_assumption: The immediate implementation of sector-specific tariffs will lead to higher input costs and reduced trade, negatively impacting corporate earnings and equity prices.
supporting_evidence: Liberation Day Apr 2025: broad reciprocal tariffs on major trading partners; sector-specific rates; immediate implementation timeline.
2018-19 US-China tariff rounds: S&P 500 -6.8% peak-to-trough over tariff escalation window; XLF and XLK underperformed.
Equity futures fell sharply overnight Apr 2 2025 — broad beta risk-off across sectors except potential short-term defensives.
transmission_channels: Trade Policy Shock → import prices → XLY margin compression
Inflation Shock → higher input costs → XLE and XLK earnings pressure
Monetary Policy Constraint → Fed boxed in (cannot ease into 7.5% CPI) → SP500 risk premium increase

channel_assessment.primary_channel: Trade Policy Shock → import prices → XLY margin compression
channel_assessment.channel_adjustments: The immediate implementation timeline and sector-specific rates amplify the negative impact on corporate earnings, which is more severe than historical trade-war analogues due to current market conditions.

environmental_technology.key_assumption: Disruption to energy infrastructure and semiconductor supply chains will lead to margin compression in the Energy and Technology sectors
supporting_evidence: Russia produces 10-11 million barrels/day oil (≈10% global supply) and exports 5M bbl/day — Europe receives ~2.5M bbl/day from Russia
Ukraine produces 70% of global neon gas supply, essential for chip lithography
CISA had issued alerts in January 2022 about Russian cyber threat escalation ahead of potential invasion
transmission_channels: Supply Chain Disruption → Energy Infrastructure disruption → XLE margin compression
Supply Chain Disruption → Semiconductor supply chain disruption → XLK margin compression
Cyber Risk → Operational disruptions → XLF, XLK, and ITA margin compression

channel_assessment.channel_adjustments: The April 2025 regime data shows moderate growth, elevated volatility, and full valuation, which increases the sensitivity of sectors to supply chain disruptions

social_behavioural.key_assumption: Retail investor sentiment is already fragile due to pre-existing inflationary concerns and a bearish AAII reading, amplifying the market's negative reaction to the tariff announcement.
supporting_evidence: AAII Sentiment Survey (Feb 2022): 46.8% Bearish – indicating a high level of pre-existing risk aversion.
Consumer Sentiment: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment 61.7 (Feb 2022) - reflecting significant inflation anxiety and reduced purchasing power.
Media Amplification Risk: Social media coverage of the Ukraine conflict combined with existing petrol pump price anxieties will accelerate behavioural overshoot.
transmission_channels: Trade Policy Shock → import prices → XLY margin compression (driven by consumer discretionary sector sensitivity)
Inflation Shock → negative real wages → AAII bearishness & retail selling
Social Amplification Risk: TikTok/Twitter coverage of the tariff announcement accelerates fear transmission and retail panic.

channel_assessment.primary_channel: Trade Policy Shock → import prices → XLY margin compression
channel_assessment.channel_adjustments: The pre-existing bearish sentiment in retail investors amplifies the negative impact of the tariff announcement on XLY, creating a more pronounced overshoot than would be expected based solely on trade policy fundamentals.

devils_advocate.key_assumption: The relief rally channel is being systematically ignored.
supporting_evidence: The VIX was 31 on Feb 23 — far above its average of 19.
